news.originalContent:
Photo by Alex Wong/Getty Images

A fake drug commercial, a show-tune parody and politicians dancing to rapper Kendrick Lamar are all part of this cycle’s artificial intelligence-powered midterm pitch to voters.

Campaigns and outside groups had spent nearly $80 million on at least 164 political ads made or enhanced with AI as of Sept. 4, the Wesleyan Media Project found. As the Nov. 3 Election Day approaches, AI ads have been used in key senate and governor races, and some have faced ridicule from critics online who call them “AI slop.”

Citizens for Sanity, a group advised by former Trump deputy White House counsel Gene Hamilton, put six figures behind an AI ad that turns Democratic Texas Senate nominee James Talarico into Julie Andrews’ beloved character, Maria, from “The Sound of Music,” the Daily Caller first reported on June 9. (RELATED: Anthropic’s AI Sent Police A False Report Of A Homicide)

The AI-generated Talarico, depicted in a video posted by the Daily Caller on X, belts out new lyrics to the musical’s number “My Favorite Things” about gender transitions for minors, which is a callback to his comment that he loves “the trans children,” in an Aug. 2, 2023, interview on A Superbloom Podcast.

Months after winning the Democratic Senate nomination over Texas Rep. Jasmine Crockett, Talarico stated on a June episode of another podcast that he opposed child sex changes.

“Boys in white dresses with blue satin sashes. Girls dosed with hormones til they grow mustaches. Changing the gender of all your offspring. These are a few of my favorite things,” the AI-generated Talarico sings.

NEW: The Trump-aligned org Citizens for Sanity is dropping a six-figure ad buy in the Texas Senate race. The ad is a 15 second clip of AI-generated James Talarico singing a "trans kids" rendition of “Favorite Things." Obtained first by @DailyCaller: https://t.co/JNY8vxYueG

“Citizens for sanity” as they make up really weird fake AI fetish videos of a man in dresses,” said one X user in response to the ad.

“Keep burning money,” Rogue DNC said on X in response to the video.

Republican New York gubernatorial nominee Bruce Blakeman posted an AI-generated attack ad to X on Sept. 1 that showed incumbent Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani in a mock drug commercial for “delusion pills.”

“Introducing Kathy, the political delusion pill for New Yorkers who would rather not think about what four more years could actually cost them,” the ad states, showing Hochul working in an outdoor garden with Mamdani.

.@KathyHochul and @ZohranKMamdani think they can cure New York’s cost-of-living crisis with excuses, empty promises, and "delusion pills." The real side effects of their policies aren’t a joke: 48 utility rate hikes, higher taxes, uncontrollable government spending, and businesses fleeing our state every single day. I have a different plan for New York. As Governor, I will deliver zero state income tax on your first $50,000, $100,000 for joint filers, cut your utility bills in half, and end the government waste. Don’t let them tax New York into the ground. Help me make New York affordable again.

State Democrats filed a Board of Elections complaint on Aug. 10, arguing Blakeman’s AI ads were “materially deceptive media,” while Blakeman, the Nassau County Executive, insisted to News10 that voters “like satire.”

The Front Line Action, a Texas super PAC, tied to Republican Texas Sen. Ted Cruz, poured upward of $90,000 into an AI-generated ad targeting Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, according to FEC filings.

Titled “Family Values,” the ad depicts an AI interpretation of El-Sayed playing a board game with his half-sister and streamer Hasan Piker as they pass around cards reading “Death to America” and “Celebrate 9/11.” In the ad, a narrator warns that “El-Sayed isn’t playing games, and his family values are wrong for Michigan.”

The ad was posted to YouTube on Sept. 11 and features women in burqas.

“[Republicans] are so desperate that they are resorting to cheap AI generated ads filled with falsehoods and bad faith attacks,” Cole Wozniak, El-Sayed’s campaign spokesman said in a statement to CNN.

Republican Tennessee Sen. Marsha Blackburn’s campaign account on X shared an AI clip Tuesday of her performing a rendition of Kendrick Lamar’s “Not Like Us,” imitating the rapper’s 2025 Super Bowl halftime performance. Dancing alongside her are fellow Tennessee Republicans Sen. Bill Hagerty, Rep. Tim Burchett, state Sen. Brent Taylor and former Knox County Mayor Glenn Jacobs, dressed as his wrestling persona Kane.

“You know, there is a county commissioner that made the video and put it up … we reposted it, and it’s a funsie. Everybody get out and vote!” Blackburn told WZTV, according to the National Desk.

Tomorrow. Ready to roll. https://t.co/YiWREmkjyx

“What in the absolute fucking AI slop is this?” an X user wrote in response to the video.

“Boomer thinks AI makes her look cool,” Adam Kinzinger, former Republican Illinois Rep wrote on X about the ad.

The ads may grab attention, but it’s unclear they change voters’ minds.

“Whether this is a complete game changer, I’m skeptical that these ads are any more persuasive than the old-fashioned political ad,” Travis Ridout, co-director of the Wesleyan Media Project, told USA Today.

Republican candidates and allied groups were behind 83 percent of AI ad spending tracked by the project. However, with no federal requirement to disclose AI use, actual spending on AI ads may be even higher.

news.originalContent:
Image not from story(Photo by Chris Hondros/Getty Images)

A Catholic priest in Ecuador was killed when a crucifix broke loose from the wall and fell on him during a Mass he was streaming live.

Father Patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari was leading a service on Saturday, Oct. 17, at Our Lady of Perpetual Help Church in Guayaquil when the heavy cross gave way, according to Newsweek. The fixture tore loose about 27 minutes into the online broadcast.

The wooden cross had hung on the wall behind the altar. Footage of the Mass captured it toppling onto the priest as he spoke to worshippers. Congregants rushed forward to help him. He died from his injuries.

The cause of the collapse remained unknown, Newsweek reported. No official statement had said whether structural damage or faulty fittings contributed. (RELATED: Rider’s Fatal Fall Captured In Rollercoaster Souvenir Photo: REPORT)

The Archdiocese of Guayaquil confirmed the priest’s death in a post on social media on Sunday. The archdiocese said he had passed into God’s presence and asked that he be granted eternal rest. It also sent condolences to his family and to his Redemptorist community.

Sánchez Molinari served as parish priest of Our Lady of Perpetual Help in the city’s Central Vicariate, according to Newsweek. He belonged to the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer, the order widely known as the Redemptorists. He streamed his Masses regularly through his own social media accounts and a YouTube channel. Earlier in his ministry he had worked in Vinces, in Los Ríos Province, according to Newseek, citing Guayaquil News.

The Italian priest St. Alphonsus Liguori founded the Redemptorist order in 1732. The congregation has long concentrated its work among poor and isolated communities. Its members now total roughly 4,500 across 82 countries.

By Sunday, the church had still offered no public account of what caused the fall, according to IBTimes.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Amir Levy/Getty Images)

Israeli officials reportedly urged Qatar for years to keep sending money into Hamas-controlled Gaza.

Letters top Israeli security officials sent to Qatari leaders show Israel pushed for and helped run a program which moved close to $2 billion into Gaza, TIME reported Sunday. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is running in Israel’s Oct. 27 national elections and was endorsed Sunday by President Donald Trump, has tried to distance himself from the payments, according to the outlet.

Letters obtained by TIME reveal Israel played a bigger role in the payments than Netanyahu has acknowledged.https://t.co/M1oyRf1mFl

Then-Mossad Director Yossi Cohen thanked Qatar’s emir, Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, in a 2020 letter for the “humanitarian aid efforts that the State of Qatar has provided the last few years to the Gaza Strip,” according to the outlet.

“Undoubtedly, these humanitarian efforts have played a crucial role in improving the humanitarian situation within the Gaza Strip, and ensuring stability and safety in the region,” Cohen wrote.

That same year, R. L. Maoz, who served on Netanyahu’s National Security Council, urged Qatari officials to keep the payments going even as the Israeli government criticized them in public, according to the outlet. “We reiterate the importance of continuing to transfer the Qatari humanitarian financial assistance through the existing mechanism,” Maoz wrote. (RELATED: Israeli Opposition Accuses Netanyahu Of Being Too Pro-Palestine)

Neither the Embassy of Israel in the United States nor the State of Qatar’s International Media Office immediately responded to the Daily Caller News Foundation’s requests for comment.

Then-Mossad Director David Barnea met with Qatari officials in September 2023, weeks before Hamas’s Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel, The New York Times reported in December 2023, citing several people familiar with the talks. Asked whether Israel wanted the payments to continue, Barnea responded affirmatively, according to the outlet.

While Netanyahu’s office did not respond to a request for comment from TIME, he told the outlet in 2024 the payments were intended to keep Gaza from collapsing. “The reason that successive governments agreed to that is that we wanted to make sure that Gaza has a functioning civilian administration to avoid humanitarian collapse,” he said.

A spokesperson for Qatar’s International Media Office, meanwhile, told TIME that all of the country’s aid went through Israel on its way into Gaza. “If any funding reached Hamas, as alleged by individuals and groups with political agendas against Qatar, the responsibility lies with Israel, which oversaw the delivery and created the mechanism,” the spokesperson reportedly said.

Qatar and several other Arab nations are working with Trump administration envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on a plan to restore Gaza’s basic services and end its reliance on armed Islamist groups, TIME reported.

news.originalSummary:

news.originalContent:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed back Sunday when NBC News’ Kristen Welker asked why President Donald Trump is “rewarding a dictator” by waiving Russia sanctions.

Bessent said on “Meet the Press” that no sanctions were lifted and that European countries are still paying Russia for its energy. Trump effectively waived a law that would have added more sanctions, Bessent said, and the only thing lifted was the embargo on Russian diesel.

“No one has been tougher on Russian sanctions than President Trump,” Bessent said, pointing to Trump’s sanctions on Rosneft and Lukoil, Russia’s two largest energy companies. (RELATED: ‘No, We Haven’t’: Chris Wright Fires Back When Asked If Trump Admin Let Americans Down At Pump)

“But you then are pushing for even tougher sanctions,” Welker countered.

“But Kristen, we did the toughest sanctions,” the secretary said as he and the NBC News host continued to talk over each other.

“But why lift them now. What has [Russian President Vladimir] Putin done to deserve sanctions relief now?” Welker asked.

“Kristen, that’s not true. No sanctions were lifted on Friday,” Bessent insisted. “No sanctions were lifted.”

“There was a law that was supposed to put more sanctions in place. The president effectively waived that,” Welker pointed out.

Trump signed an executive order Friday waiving the Russian sanctions and tariffs required under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which he signed into law Sept. 18.

The law, named for the late Republican South Carolina Sen. Lindsey Graham, directs the president to impose tariffs of up to 100 percent on goods from the top five importers of Russian oil and gas and up to 500 percent on goods imported from Russia. The Senate passed it 86-11 on Aug. 7, and the House passed it 262-159 in September.

Bessent again ensured Welker that “no sanctions were lifted,” and that the “only thing that has been lifted was the diesel embargo.”

Also during the exchange, Welker told Bessent that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had told her the move “is a big support for Putin” and asked, “Why is the president rewarding a dictator who invaded Ukraine?”

“President Trump has made it clear he wants the killing to stop,” Bessent responded, adding that the law gives the president 60 days to assess the situation.

He then turned to Europe, saying European countries have given Russia Putin more money than they have given Ukraine.

“They continue to gorge on Russian energy,” Bessent said. (RELATED: Trump’s Diesel Deal With Putin Runs Into The Ban Congress Passed On Russian Energy)

The secretary said 136 of the 140 cargoes that left one Russian facility in the first six months of the year went to Europe, worth more than $8 billion. He said he asked European allies in the spring to join the U.S. in putting secondary tariffs on China and India and that they refused. “So why should the U.S. bear the burden?” he asked.

Welker then played a clip from Bessent’s January 2025 confirmation hearing, in which he said the Biden administration had been worried about raising U.S. energy prices during an election season. “Is President Trump doing what you accused President Biden of doing?” she asked.

“Kristen, the sanctions were double the Biden administration in an act of incredible bravery,” he replied. “Double the sanctions on the way out in January 2025.”

Bessent also said during the interview that the United Kingdom waived its own embargo on diesel and jet fuel made with Russian crude in May, asking, “where’s the outrage for the rest of the world?”

“The Europeans are financing the Russian war machine,” he added.

Bessent again ensured Welker that “no sanctions were lifted,” and that the “only thing that has been lifted was the diesel embargo.”

Also during the exchange, Welker told Bessent that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had told her the move “is a big support for Putin” and asked, “Why is the president rewarding a dictator who invaded Ukraine?”

“President Trump has made it clear he wants the killing to stop,” Bessent responded, adding that the law gives the president 60 days to assess the situation.

He then turned to Europe, saying European countries have given Russia Putin more money than they have given Ukraine.

“They continue to gorge on Russian energy,” Bessent said. (RELATED: Trump’s Diesel Deal With Putin Runs Into The Ban Congress Passed On Russian Energy)

The secretary said 136 of the 140 cargoes that left one Russian facility in the first six months of the year went to Europe, worth more than $8 billion. He said he asked European allies in the spring to join the U.S. in putting secondary tariffs on China and India and that they refused. “So why should the U.S. bear the burden?” he asked.

Welker then played a clip from Bessent’s January 2025 confirmation hearing, in which he said the Biden administration had been worried about raising U.S. energy prices during an election season. “Is President Trump doing what you accused President Biden of doing?” she asked.

“Kristen, the sanctions were double the Biden administration in an act of incredible bravery,” he replied. “Double the sanctions on the way out in January 2025.”

Bessent also said during the interview that the United Kingdom waived its own embargo on diesel and jet fuel made with Russian crude in May, asking, “where’s the outrage for the rest of the world?”

“The Europeans are financing the Russian war machine,” he added.

news.originalContent:
Photo by Garry Austin/Getty Images

Parents accused a youth sports travel company of misleading families into paying hotel booking fees and higher lodging costs by telling them their children could not compete unless they booked through its platform, according to a federal lawsuit.

The proposed class action against Team Travel Source challenges “stay-to-play” practices that tie tournament participation to designated hotel booking arrangements, adding to the costs families face beyond registration, equipment and travel. Attorney Karen Dahlberg O’Connell told the Daily Caller News Foundation that hundreds of parents contacted her legal team after the case was filed, reporting similar experiences across the country.

The lawsuit, filed in the Western District of Kentucky against The Complete Plan Inc., which operates as Team Travel Source, includes nine parents from seven states whose children participate in cheerleading and volleyball. The amended complaint alleges deceptive booking requirements, inadequately disclosed mandatory fees and misleading promises of discounted hotel rates.

Team Travel Source denied wrongdoing in a statement provided to the DCNF by Kelley Roberts.

“We deny participation in any alleged violation of the law in connection with the allegations in the proposed class action lawsuit or otherwise,” the company said, adding that it would address the allegations through counsel in the appropriate forum. “We have always run our company in an ethical way and truly appreciate everyone in the space.”

In court filings seeking dismissal, the company argued that tournament organizers established stay-to-play requirements and determine exemptions. It also said its checkout process disclosed fees before customers finalized reservations and that families received services including room blocks, booking assistance and customer support.

Kentucky mother Kate Russell alleged she booked three nights at an Atlanta hotel for $516.85, including $15 in booking service fees, after being told her daughter’s volleyball team could be disqualified if she did not reserve through the platform. A teammate’s family booked elsewhere and the child still competed, according to the complaint.

The parents also challenged mandatory charges labeled as booking, housing, cancellation convenience and premier property fees. Some applied per night even when a parent made a single reservation, the complaint alleges.

The company’s guarantee applies only to some events, excludes booking fees from rate comparisons and requires matching room types, amenities and cancellation terms. Membership and government rates are among its exclusions.

O’Connell described one parent who reported finding a cheaper room directly through a hotel but was denied an adjustment because the Team Travel Source reservation guaranteed access to a rollaway bed. The parent neither wanted nor needed that bed, O’Connell said.

The amended complaint also cites company marketing claiming more than $17 million in rebates paid to tournament organizers in 2025. Plaintiffs allege those payments were funded by inflated lodging costs and fees; that funding allegation remains disputed.

The company’s reach extended to more than 1,600 annual events in over 400 cities across 44 states, according to website figures cited in the complaint.

An Aspen Institute survey found families spent an average of $1,016 on one child’s primary sport in 2024, up 46% from 2019.

“I just want parents to have the freedom of choice in terms of how they stay and where they stay,” O’Connell told the DCNF.

The parents seek class certification, damages and court orders addressing the challenged practices. Team Travel Source asked the court to dismiss the amended complaint and filed its reply supporting that request on Wednesday.

news.originalContent:
با رای اعتماد نمایندگان مجلس مهرداد اخلاقی کتابچی وزیر دفاع ایران شد. او از مدیران با سابقه صنایع دفاعی و هوافضای در جمهوری اسلامی است اما تاکنون چهره‌ای کمتر شناخته‌شده برای عموم بوده است.

او  در نشست وبیناری علنی مجلس با ۲۳۷ رأی موافق، جایگزین عزیز نصیرزاده شد که با ۲۸۱ رای رکورد بالاترین رای اعتماد تاریخ جمهوری اسلامی را داشت اما در اولین روز جنگ ۴۰ روزه همراه چند فرمانده ارشد کشته شد.

در جلسه رای اعتماد، مسعود پزشکیان، رئیس جمهور، از آقای اخلاقی به عنوان فردی یاد کرد که سابقه همکاری با حسن تهرانی مقدم، محسن فخری‌زاده و امیرعلی حاجی‌زاده را داشته است و افزود که او در «لیست ترور» قرار داد.

حسن تهرانی مقدم و محسن فخری زاده که از اولی به عنوان «پدر برنامه موشکی» و دومی به عنوان «پدر برنامه هسته‌ای» ایران نام برده می‌شود، در سال‌های ۱۳۹۰ و ۱۳۹۹ ترور شدند. امیرعلی حاجی‌زاده، فرمانده هوافضای سپاه هم  در جنگ ۱۲ روزه در حمله اسرائیل کشته شد.

رئیس‌جمهور ایران با اشاره به «۴۲ سال» سابقه آقای اخلاقی گفت همین که او مدت‌هاست در فهرست «ترور» است و آمریکا هم او را تحریم کرده است، نشانه صلاحیت اوست.

مهرداد اخلاقی کتابچی در دفاع از خود گفت: «پس از جنگ ۱۲ روزه، قابلیت‌های دفاعی به‌گونه‌ای روزآمد شده‌اند که برآوردها و محاسبات دشمن را تغییر داده و تردیدی عمیق در میان دشمنان درباره استمرار جنگ ایجاد کرده‌اند.»

مهرداد اخلاقی اگرچه برای رسانه‌ها چهره‌ای ناشناس بود اما آمریکا ۱۹ سال پیش او را در فهرست تحریم‌هایش قرار داده بود. آقای پزشکیان امروز گفت‌ تحریم‌ شدن او خود دلیل صلاحیتش است.

نام آقای اخلاقی در قطعنامه ۱۷۴۷ شورای امنیت سازمان ملل متحد  ایران هم ذکر شده است. در آن قطعنامه از کشورهای دنیا خواسته شده‌ ارتباط با شرکت‌های ایرانی فعال در انرژی هسته‌ای را محدود کنند

ساعتی پس از رای اعتماد مجلس، احمد وحیدی، فرمانده کل سپاه پاسداران و امیر حاتمی، فرمانده ارتش انتخاب او را تبریک گفتند و از او حمایت کردند.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

وقتی نام مهرداد اخلاقی به عنوان وزیر دفاع جدید ایران مطرح شد، عکسی در رسانه‌ها نداشت.

۲۱ مهر زمانی که در کمیسیون ویژه مجلس برای رسیدگی به صلاحیتش حاضر شد، شماری از رسانه‌های ایران با تیتر ‌«اولین تصویر از مهرداد اخلاقی کتابچی» این جلسه را پوشش دادند.

او بر خلاف مجید ابن‌الرضا، سرپرست وقت وزارت دفاع، که با عنوان و یونیفرم نظامی در مراسم حاضر می‌شود، با کت‌وشلوار به جلسه کمیسیون ویژه رفته بود.

آقای اخلاقی کتابچی متولد ۱۳۳۷ است و بنا به گزارش کمیسیون امنیت ملی و سیاست خارجی مجلس شورای اسلامی، مدرک کارشناسی مهندسی شیمی از دانشگاه صنعتی امیرکبیر و کارشناسی ارشد مدیریت راهبردی از دانشگاه صنعتی مالک اشتر دارد.

او مدتی ریاست گروه صنعتی شهید باقری را بر عهده داشته که در طراحی و توسعه و تولید سامانه‌های موشکی از جمله موشک‌های بالستیک فعالیت می‌کرده است.

آقای اخلاقی در آبان ۱۳۹۳، در دولت حسن روحانی، با حکم حسین دهقان، وزیر وقت دفاع، به عنوان مدیرعامل سازمان صنایع هوافضای وزارت دفاع (ساصد) منصوب شد.

دفاع‌پرس که اخبار نظامی ایران را پوشش می‌دهد از آقای اخلاقی به عنوان چهره‌ای یاد کرده است که در توسعه ظرفیت‌های موشکی ایران نقش داشته و در در ‌«حوزه پیشران‌های سوخت جامد» جایگاه ویژه‌ای داشته است.

پیشران‌های سوخت جامد، در توسعه برنامه موشک‌های بالستیک ایران و به طور خاص افزایش برد، آمادگی عملیاتی و کاهش زمان آماده‌سازی و پرتاب نقشی اساسی داشته است.

مهرداد اخلاقی در بخشی از معرفی خود گفته بود از سال ۱۳۶۳ تا ۱۳۷۳ صرفا در حوزه تحقیقات فعالیت داشته و از سال ۱۳۷۳ وارد بخش تولید شده است.

آقای اخلاقی ارائه جزئیات برنامه‌هایش به مجلس را به مصلحت امنیتی نداست اما تاکید کرد که طبقه‌بندی سری، سازه‌های امن برای تولید محصولات و حمایت از جبهه مقاومت تاکید کرد.

آقای اخلاقی وعده داده که توسعه توان موشکی به ویژه موشک‌های زمین به زمین و کروز و همچنین پدافند را در اولویت برنامه‌هایش قرار دهد.

او همچنین گفت که اولین جنگنده سنگین که کاملا ساخت ایران است سال آینده به پرواز در‌آید.

مهرداد اخلاقی در بخشی از توضیحات خودش به مجلس گفت: «از ۹ اسفند [آغاز حمله آمریکا و اسرائیل به ایران] تا امروز، محل کار من در سازمان صنایع دفاع در مجاورت ساختمان‌هایی بود که مورد اصابت موشک قرار گرفته بودند. با وجود اصابت ۲۵ موشک به ساختمان محل کارم، حتی از فاصله ۱۰۰متری آن نیز خارج نشدم و محل استقرارم را تغییر ندادم.»

مجتبی خامنه‌ای اخیر در پیامی از فرماندهان نظامی ایران علی الخصوص فرمانده هوافضا سپاه خواسته بود تا امنیت خود را در اولویت قرار دهند.

او در پیام مرداد ماه خود خطاب به مجید موسوی، فرمانده نیروی هوافضای سپاه، نوشته بود: که «مراقبت از جان عزیز خودتان و همه برادران خواسته مؤکد اینجانب است.»

یکی از نخستین اظهارات مهرداد اخلاقی در حاشیه جلسه رای اعتماد مجلس در پاسخ خبرنگاران درباره احتمال استفاده آمریکا از «مادر بمب‌ها» بود که گفت:

«ما تدابیر لازم را برای این موضوع اندیشیده‌ایم و خیالمان راحت است. با اطمینان کار خود را انجام می‌دهیم.»

او گفت که رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا «باید به فکر این باشد که نیروهایش را سالم از منطقه ما خارج کند. اگر یک بمب بیندازد، باید ببیند چند نفر از نیروهایش را باید به‌صورت افقی از منطقه خارج کند.»

به گفته وزیر دفاع جدید ایران، «همین موضوع باعث شده است که آمریکا تاکنون از این اقدام خودداری کند. البته اگر تهدیدهایش را از شعار به عمل تبدیل کند، نتیجه‌اش را خواهد دید.»

ساعتی پس از رای اعتماد مجلس، احمد وحیدی، فرمانده کل سپاه پاسداران و امیر حاتمی، فرمانده ارتش انتخاب او را تبریک گفتند و از او حمایت کردند.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

وقتی نام مهرداد اخلاقی به عنوان وزیر دفاع جدید ایران مطرح شد، عکسی در رسانه‌ها نداشت.

۲۱ مهر زمانی که در کمیسیون ویژه مجلس برای رسیدگی به صلاحیتش حاضر شد، شماری از رسانه‌های ایران با تیتر ‌«اولین تصویر از مهرداد اخلاقی کتابچی» این جلسه را پوشش دادند.

او بر خلاف مجید ابن‌الرضا، سرپرست وقت وزارت دفاع، که با عنوان و یونیفرم نظامی در مراسم حاضر می‌شود، با کت‌وشلوار به جلسه کمیسیون ویژه رفته بود.

آقای اخلاقی کتابچی متولد ۱۳۳۷ است و بنا به گزارش کمیسیون امنیت ملی و سیاست خارجی مجلس شورای اسلامی، مدرک کارشناسی مهندسی شیمی از دانشگاه صنعتی امیرکبیر و کارشناسی ارشد مدیریت راهبردی از دانشگاه صنعتی مالک اشتر دارد.

او مدتی ریاست گروه صنعتی شهید باقری را بر عهده داشته که در طراحی و توسعه و تولید سامانه‌های موشکی از جمله موشک‌های بالستیک فعالیت می‌کرده است.

آقای اخلاقی در آبان ۱۳۹۳، در دولت حسن روحانی، با حکم حسین دهقان، وزیر وقت دفاع، به عنوان مدیرعامل سازمان صنایع هوافضای وزارت دفاع (ساصد) منصوب شد.

دفاع‌پرس که اخبار نظامی ایران را پوشش می‌دهد از آقای اخلاقی به عنوان چهره‌ای یاد کرده است که در توسعه ظرفیت‌های موشکی ایران نقش داشته و در در ‌«حوزه پیشران‌های سوخت جامد» جایگاه ویژه‌ای داشته است.

پیشران‌های سوخت جامد، در توسعه برنامه موشک‌های بالستیک ایران و به طور خاص افزایش برد، آمادگی عملیاتی و کاهش زمان آماده‌سازی و پرتاب نقشی اساسی داشته است.

مهرداد اخلاقی در بخشی از معرفی خود گفته بود از سال ۱۳۶۳ تا ۱۳۷۳ صرفا در حوزه تحقیقات فعالیت داشته و از سال ۱۳۷۳ وارد بخش تولید شده است.

آقای اخلاقی ارائه جزئیات برنامه‌هایش به مجلس را به مصلحت امنیتی نداست اما تاکید کرد که طبقه‌بندی سری، سازه‌های امن برای تولید محصولات و حمایت از جبهه مقاومت تاکید کرد.

آقای اخلاقی وعده داده که توسعه توان موشکی به ویژه موشک‌های زمین به زمین و کروز و همچنین پدافند را در اولویت برنامه‌هایش قرار دهد.

او همچنین گفت که اولین جنگنده سنگین که کاملا ساخت ایران است سال آینده به پرواز در‌آید.

مهرداد اخلاقی در بخشی از توضیحات خودش به مجلس گفت: «از ۹ اسفند [آغاز حمله آمریکا و اسرائیل به ایران] تا امروز، محل کار من در سازمان صنایع دفاع در مجاورت ساختمان‌هایی بود که مورد اصابت موشک قرار گرفته بودند. با وجود اصابت ۲۵ موشک به ساختمان محل کارم، حتی از فاصله ۱۰۰متری آن نیز خارج نشدم و محل استقرارم را تغییر ندادم.»

مجتبی خامنه‌ای اخیر در پیامی از فرماندهان نظامی ایران علی الخصوص فرمانده هوافضا سپاه خواسته بود تا امنیت خود را در اولویت قرار دهند.

او در پیام مرداد ماه خود خطاب به مجید موسوی، فرمانده نیروی هوافضای سپاه، نوشته بود: که «مراقبت از جان عزیز خودتان و همه برادران خواسته مؤکد اینجانب است.»

یکی از نخستین اظهارات مهرداد اخلاقی در حاشیه جلسه رای اعتماد مجلس در پاسخ خبرنگاران درباره احتمال استفاده آمریکا از «مادر بمب‌ها» بود که گفت:

«ما تدابیر لازم را برای این موضوع اندیشیده‌ایم و خیالمان راحت است. با اطمینان کار خود را انجام می‌دهیم.»

او گفت که رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا «باید به فکر این باشد که نیروهایش را سالم از منطقه ما خارج کند. اگر یک بمب بیندازد، باید ببیند چند نفر از نیروهایش را باید به‌صورت افقی از منطقه خارج کند.»

به گفته وزیر دفاع جدید ایران، «همین موضوع باعث شده است که آمریکا تاکنون از این اقدام خودداری کند. البته اگر تهدیدهایش را از شعار به عمل تبدیل کند، نتیجه‌اش را خواهد دید.»

news.originalContent:
(Photo by ATTA KENARE / AFP via Getty Images)

U.S. military strikes on Iran could rapidly intensify soon, a senior military official exclusively told the Daily Caller News Foundation.

While American strikes on Iran appear to have reduced in frequency and intensity as the Trump administration braces for midterms, that could quickly change, a senior military official familiar with the matter granted anonymity to speak told the DCNF. To that point, the U.S. military is currently conducting a massive force buildup in the region.

“Things are about to get spicy,” the senior military official told the DCNF. (RELATED: ‘War Criminal’: Iran War Protestors Scream At Hegseth While Being Dragged Out Of Event)

Approximately 9,000 additional sailors and Marines are deploying to the region aboard the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group and USS Makin Island amphibious ready group, potentially enhancing the regional American naval presence to more than 20,000 personnel and three aircraft carriers by late October, The Associated Press reported, citing a U.S. official.

(Photo by AHMAD AL-RUBAYE / AFP via Getty Images)

American aerial refueling flights over the Middle East likewise increased approximately 50% per day during the first two weeks of October compared to September, alongside a significant increase in military transport aircraft activity, according to an open-source flight-tracking analysis published by IntelSky.

“Of course this buildup could be a direct preparation for already planned actions,” Steve Bucci, a retired Army colonel and visiting fellow at the Heritage Foundation’s Phillip N. Truluck Center for Leadership Development, told the DCNF. “It is more than likely a signal and a threat, with the hope it will not be needed, but with a full readiness to use it.” (RELATED: Iranian Strikes On US Military Bases Took Massive Toll, Pentagon Watchdog Reveals)

“Iran’s attempt to establish their own deterrence against the West, and the U.S.’s attempt to do the same via its own military buildup will merely contribute to greater escalation and another round of conflict, which is inevitable,” Barak Seener, an associate research fellow at the Henry Jackson Society and founder of Strategic Intelligentia, also told the Daily Caller News Foundation. “The only question is when - before or after the midterms?”

“The influx of fighter squadrons and carrier groups required to replace exhausted missile defense stockpiles is likely to contribute to the next phase of escalation rather than reestablish deterrence,” he added. “On the contrary, Iranian threats to global commerce in the Strait of Hormuz [are] an attempt by the Iranian regime to establish their deterrence against the West from targeting the regime.”

Senior White House aides have reportedly sought to prevent a major escalation of the Iran war ahead of the Nov. 3, 2026, midterm elections. While officials could consider intensifying military operations after Americans head to the polls, no final decision on renewing large-scale strikes has been made, Reuters reported Sept. 2, citing four people familiar with internal discussions.

“It appears that Trump and Hegseth are planning another round of bombing Iran, which may actually happen before the midterm U.S. elections,” a Veterans for Peace spokesperson told the DCNF. “There is talk about dropping the ‘Mother Of All Bombs’ (MOAB), the most powerful ‘conventional’ weapon, or even dropping nuclear bombs! This will only cause more death, destruction and destabilization in the Middle East and worldwide.”

“I don’t believe that President Trump is taking any options off the table,” Alex Welz, a senior research associate for the Middle East and North Africa at the Heritage Foundation, told the DCNF. “He has publicly weighed the idea of reengaging in kinetic strikes but has also voiced hope for a diplomatic resolution. U.S. military deployments are essential in either case: to engage Iran in a limited, precise fashion, or to maintain a credible force posture against any Iranian threats.”

(Photo by ATTA KENARE / AFP via Getty Images)

Iran has intensified attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz, striking at least 24 vessels between Sept. 28 and Oct. 11 despite American strikes against its military infrastructure, according to an Oct. 14 Institute for the Study of War assessment. Two additional cargo vessels sank in the strait Oct. 14. Meanwhile, Iranian forces have increasingly relied on small boats and human spotters to identify targets following American strikes on their coastal radar systems, Reuters reported, citing a U.S. military official.

The Iranian strikes may be a result of President Donald Trump’s recent statements threatening to “annihilate” the Islamic regime.

“I have a big decision to make,” Trump said Sept. 22 while addressing the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly, including whether he would “annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly.”

“In my view, it is impossible to opine sensibly as to what President Trump will do next,” J.D. Foster, a former senior fellow on the economics of fiscal policy at The Heritage Foundation, told the DCNF. “He’s put himself in a deep hole and all he knows how to do is dig deeper. He has recreated Vietnam 1968 to a fair approximation, except there’s no Haiphong Harbor to mine.”

“There is every indication that the U.S. military is prepared to escalate if that’s what the president orders,” Matthew Kyle Sharp, a senior nuclear fellow at the Center for Nuclear Security Policy within the Massachusetts Institute of Technology’s (MIT) Security Studies Program, told the DCNF. “These preparations could also seek to deter Iranian escalation, or alternatively to generate pressure in support of negotiations. Threats of military escalation may be deemed necessary to close wide gaps between the two sides in terms of diplomacy.”

Iran, for its part, offered to open the Strait of Hormuz just a few days before Trump made that declaration.

Tehran told Washington it could reopen the critical waterway within seven days if the United States eased military pressure and lifted its blockade on Iranian ports, Reuters reported, citing a senior Iranian official. Iran delivered the proposal through mediators Sept. 16 and said its delegation in New York had authority to revive diplomacy, according to the outlet.

Some experts, however, said the possibility of an escalation in the Iran War is directly linked to Israel and its upcoming elections.

“As was the case when Trump first initiated his war of choice on Iran, a reignition of the war would begin with the Israelis leading the attack and the U.S. being sucked in,” Steve Hanke, a professor of applied economics at Johns Hopkins University who served on President Reagan’s Council of Economic Advisers, told the DCNF. “If this happens, the Iranians will counterattack and destroy all that remains of the oil infrastructure on the western side of the Persian Gulf as well as its vital desalination plants.”

“The buildup may be a deterrent aimed at adding credibility to Trump’s threats to attack after the midterms but it is having the opposite effect and may prompt Iran to preempt a potential U.S. attack before the election,” Jamal Abdi, the president of the National Iranian American Council (NIAC), told the DCNF. “Trump wants to hold off until after U.S. elections but Netanyahu may want strikes before his own election and Iranian officials have made clear they will not be second to strike.”

Likewise, the recent reduction in strikes on Iran by the U.S. military could also be tied to polling showing the Iran War is largely unpopular among Americans. (RELATED: Tehran Dangles Peace Deal Hours Before Trump Threatens To ‘Annihilate’ Iran)

(Photo by ATTA KENARE / AFP via Getty Images)

Sixty-four percent of respondents identified the conflict as one of their top voting considerations, according to an Oct. 15 Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research poll. The survey asked respondents to rate the importance of issues — including the war with Iran — when considering their vote in the upcoming election. Conducted Oct. 8-12 among 1,119 American adults, the poll carries an overall margin of error of plus or minus 3.9 percentage points.

In addition, approximately 65% of respondents disapprove of President Trump’s handling of military operations against Iran, while 33% approve, according to an Oct. 8 Pew Research Center poll. Conducted by SSRS for Pew from Sept. 28 to Oct. 4, the poll surveyed a total of 5,062 American adults. Only 2,527 respondents received the Iran question, however, resulting in a margin of error of plus or minus 2.3 percentage points for that subgroup.

“The U.S. president has indicated desperation and frustration, and has threatened escalation and even nuclear escalation (nothing less would eliminate a whole civilization etc [sic]). Continuing the war or ending it as things stand is a political disaster for him,” World Beyond War Executive Director David Swanson told the DCNF. “Some leading Democrats and many media outlets, rather than pressing him to end the war, have focused on denouncing what ever deal he might make to do so. Obviously any deal will be worse for Trump and Western oil companies than never having created the war or never having torn up the previous deal.”

(Photo by Majid Saeedi/Getty Images)

Meanwhile, 69% of Americans believe the war in Iran has not been worth fighting, while 71% disapprove of Trump’s handling of the conflict, according to an Oct. 1 Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research poll. Conducted from Sept. 24-28 among 2,140 American adults, the poll carries a margin of error of plus or minus 2.9 percentage points.

“The Pentagon is facing big holes in its supply of key munitions, doubling down on the Iran war will put increased pressure on shortfalls of interceptors and certain missiles,” Abdi told the DCNF. “The President will need Congress to replenish supplies, but if Democrats win Congressional majorities, there will be enormous pressure to cut funding necessary to continue the war and to rearm.”

The survey asked respondents to rate the importance of issues — including the war with Iran — when considering their vote in the upcoming election. Conducted Oct. 8-12 among 1,119 American adults, the poll carries an overall margin of error of plus or minus 3.9 percentage points.

In addition, approximately 65% of respondents disapprove of President Trump’s handling of military operations against Iran, while 33% approve, according to an Oct. 8 Pew Research Center poll. Conducted by SSRS for Pew from Sept. 28 to Oct. 4, the poll surveyed a total of 5,062 American adults. Only 2,527 respondents received the Iran question, however, resulting in a margin of error of plus or minus 2.3 percentage points for that subgroup.

“The U.S. president has indicated desperation and frustration, and has threatened escalation and even nuclear escalation (nothing less would eliminate a whole civilization etc [sic]). Continuing the war or ending it as things stand is a political disaster for him,” World Beyond War Executive Director David Swanson told the DCNF. “Some leading Democrats and many media outlets, rather than pressing him to end the war, have focused on denouncing what ever deal he might make to do so. Conducted from Sept. 24-28 among 2,140 American adults, the poll carries a margin of error of plus or minus 2.9 percentage points.

“The Pentagon is facing big holes in its supply of key munitions, doubling down on the Iran war will put increased pressure on shortfalls of interceptors and certain missiles,” Abdi told the DCNF. “The President will need Congress to replenish supplies, but if Democrats win Congressional majorities, there will be enormous pressure to cut funding necessary to continue the war and to rearm.”

news.originalContent: The IDF addressed the strikes carried out overnight in southern Lebanon, including in the village of Kfar Reman, saying on Monday afternoon that they began after Hezbollah terrorists launched two explosive drones at Israeli forces on the Ali Taher ridge in southern Lebanon. No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility.   No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility. A vehicle in which two people were killed. The Associated Press reported that the vehicle belonged to the Lebanese Scout and Rescue Association, Al-Risala, and that one of those killed was a paramedic with the organization. Two other people were wounded. At the same time, Lebanese reports said a building in Kfar Reman where a large number of people were staying was also struck, killing nine people, including women and children, and wounding 11 others.   Prior to the strikes, steps were taken to mitigate harm to uninvolved individuals, including the use of precise munitions and aerial surveillance," the IDF said in response. "The claim that several uninvolved individuals were harmed as a result of the strikes is being reviewed.” The IDF said that, in addition, following the launch of the explosive drones Sunday, “the IDF struck in the Nabatieh area and eliminated several Hezbollah terrorists. "The IDF will not allow the Hezbollah terrorist organization to harm Israeli civilians or IDF soldiers and will continue to operate to remove threats while remaining committed to the ceasefire agreement." “We lived under constant intimidation because of the bombardments on the outskirts of the village,” Fouad Chakroun, a resident of Kfar Reman told AP as he stood in front of the destroyed building. “Now they have struck the heart of the village.” Another resident, Saleh Madlij, said families and children had been staying in the building. “Are there missiles here?” he said sarcastically. “I will not leave this place.” The BBC reported that, according to Lebanese media, seven additional people were killed in strikes Sunday, while Lebanese President Joseph Aoun warned that the attacks represented a “dangerous escalation” that threatened the ceasefire.

news.title: Israel's public diplomacy 'never been worse', officials say

According to them, the situation only worsens, and the support the world has shown Israel following Hamas’s attack on October 7 has already been forgotten. According to them, the situation only worsens, and the support the world has shown Israel following Hamas’s attack on October 7 has already been forgotten. Ministers in the government blame Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the complete neglect of Israel’s public relations: "There’s no leader present it’s been abandoned. A pandemic of sanctions against Israel may break out, and if we don't wake up, it will be too late. Something big needed to be done in terms of public relations, we need to rally the Jewish people and launch an international campaign. There’s no leader to head this. We’re losing. Our friends tell us: we support you, but you’re losing in the court of public opinion." A senior figure in Israel's advocacy efforts added, "They neutralized the Foreign Ministry and took away all its budget. The Foreign Ministry has no funding. To this day, no money was delivered. We’re working with a budget of 2 million shekels allocated for the war since the beginning of the year.  “Each U.S. consulate receives $5,000 a year for public relations efforts, including Independence Day events. For example, the consulate in Boston, which is also responsible for MIT, has to struggle to have such an amount. It’s ridiculous. When you already have a talented spokesman like Eylon Levy, they unjustly suspend him. He was one of the few people who did his mission in the most talented, beautiful, and correct way, and they sent him home,” the source said.   Internal reports from Israeli missions in the United States describe a very harsh picture of Israeli coverage in the American media. One report described, "The media awaited a sign from the government for a policy change, and when it arrived - it unleashed a rampage and published constant harsh criticism against Israel that had always existed. The harsh reports from Gaza, alongside internal tensions in the U.S., threaten to push moderate writers from the mainstream to adopt critical positions toward Israel and demand an immediate and permanent cease-fire.” 'the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy' “Pressure on the Biden administration to harden its stance toward Israel and condition military aid for an Israeli policy change constitutes a warning sign for the future,” the report added. “In terms of 'color,' we’re currently in a 'dark orange.' “There’s a change in stances even among staunch supporters of Israel – and while the conservative media fully supported Israel's actions in the past, this time voices questioning the proportionality of Israeli action have also been heard. However, no demand for a cease-fire is expected to appear in those media outlets. Without a fundamental change in the humanitarian issue in Gaza and/or signs on the diplomatic solution on the horizon, criticism of Israel in the media is expected to intensify,” the report read. It was added, "In the last month, the U.S. media’s spotlight turned to the worsening humanitarian crisis in Gaza, with special emphasis given to the suffering of Rafah residents against the backdrop of the possibility of the IDF expanding the ground operation there as well. Leading media outlets flooded screens and front pages with images of starving children, trauma victims, and the destruction of homes and hospitals. Reports and personal stories from Rafah led to empathy toward the Palestinians’ suffering and anger toward Israel's military actions. "Although most media outlets refrained from blaming Israel for creating the crisis intentionally or denying its right to self-defense, opinion pieces sparked fierce debate regarding the proportionality and morality of the ongoing military operation in its current form. Critical voices that were once silenced now have a wider platform.    “Reports focused on the immense humanitarian damages and the harm to innocent civilians, which many analysts argue is unjustified and goes against the values of the IDF’s operation. Even publicists who supported Israel in the past admitted that the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy,” the report read. “Against this backdrop, a narrative is emerging among liberal authors, which sees the Biden administration and its policy of providing weapons and diplomatic support to Israel as responsible for the situation, or at least as someone who can bring it to an end." Furthermore, dozens of recent opinion pieces represent a wide range of positions regarding the IDF’s legitimacy, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, the question of a cease-fire, and the future of U.S.-Israel relations: Conservative media outlets like The Wall Street Journal and The New York Post fully support Israel, advocate for continued military action against Hamas, and refrain from calling for an immediate and prolonged stop to the war.  In contrast, newspapers identified with the center and liberal left, including The New York Times and The Washington Post, criticize the war’s escalation, citing the destructive consequences of the confrontation on Palestinian civilians, and therefore calling for an immediate humanitarian cease-fire, the reports explained.   The reports also expose an erosion of Israel's standing in Washington against the backdrop of the escalation in the Gaza war. This was clearly reflected in U.S. President Joe Biden's statement regarding a "red line" on military operations in Rafah, and Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech.  Most analysts don’t foresee an immediate shift in relations between the countries, but caution against potential political damage to both sides. Furthermore, calls are increasing to use American military aid to Israel as leverage to force policy change in Jerusalem. However, warnings have been raised that the fact of having this discussion could bolster Hamas's position and undermine the chances of a cease-fire.  While conservative media outlets present Israel's policy as legitimate self-defense, liberal media outlets provide a platform for writers who echo the Palestinian narrative, sometimes using rhetoric accusing Israel of "apartheid" and even "genocide." Calls for the U.S. government to distance itself from supporting Israel and reconsider its military aid plan are becoming more common, even in moderate media outlets. The report mentions articles in The Washington Post and The Daily Beast highlighting the effectiveness of pro-Palestinian activists in influencing public opinion in the U.S., especially among progressive Democratic voters. The articles point to growing discontent with the Biden administration's support for Israel, reflected in "Uncommitted" votes in the Democratic primaries and disruptions at party events. Tactics such as demanding a cease-fire and using the term "genocide" have succeeded in keeping the war at the forefront of the national political agenda and increasing pressure on Washington to minimize its support of Israel.  The increasing willingness of Democratic politicians to criticize Israel suggests a shift in the party's traditional stance and leads to speech free of restraint in media outlets as well. This trend reached its zenith with Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech, in which he labeled Netanyahu an "obstacle to peace" and accused him of damaging Israel's international standing, calling for early Israeli elections.

news.originalSummary: Rather than celebrating and resting over the three-day holiday, residents of the Jewish community of Hendon in north London and Radlett were struck by shock and grief after the deadly terror attack that took the lives of two daughters of their beloved and esteemed Rabbi Leo Dee, on Friday, the second day of Passover which is considered a holly day in diaspora communities. news.originalContent: Rather than celebrating and resting over the three-day holiday, residents of the Jewish community of Hendon in north London and Radlett were struck by shock and grief after the deadly terror attack that took the lives of two daughters of their beloved and esteemed Rabbi Leo Dee, on Friday, the second day of Passover which is considered a holly day in diaspora communities.   Follow Ynetnews on Facebook and Twitter >> Related stories: Israel names two sisters killed in West Bank terror attack At least one dead and six injured in a terror attack in Tel Aviv Family loses two daughters to deadly terror attack Members of the Jewish London community, including friends of the family, who heard of the devastating news after the Shabbat ended, were confronted only then, with the horrific reports of Maia and Rina's death. The funerals for the Dee sisters will be held today at the Kfar Etzion Cemetery.   Rabbi Leo Dee served as the Assistant Rabbi at the Hendon United Synagogue in North London from 2008-2011, and as the Senior Rabbi at Radlett United Synagogue from 2011-2014, after which the family made aliyah. They were a much beloved and respected family in the UK Jewish community. “People feel shock and disappointment. The family were communal people and served their communities well and were well-liked.” said a former member of the congregation at Hendon United Synagogue who did not wish to be named.  “I feel sick seeing this… good people who would never hurt anyone, murdered. I can't imagine his anguish, and pray Lucy survives,” said Joseph, another former congregant.   Chief UK Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis laments the death of the British-Israeli girls murdered in Friday's terror strike on the West Bank.  In a statement, the rabbi said: "No words can describe the depth of our shock and sadness at the heartbreaking news of the murder by terrorists in Israel of Maya & Rina Dee, daughters of Rebbetzen Lucy, who is in a critical condition & Rabbi Leo Dee, my dear colleagues. He continued, “They were much loved in the Hendon and Radlett communities in the UK, as well as in Israel and well beyond.” UK statement not mentioning terrorism The British Board of Deputies also issued a statement expressing shock over the tragic attack: “We are deeply shocked and saddened at the murder by Palestinian terrorists of Maia and Rina Dee, the daughters of Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee formerly of Radlett United Synagogue. We wish Lucy Refuah Shlemah and long life to the family as they cope with this devastating news.” Palestinian terrorist shot and killed 2 British-Israeli nationals, also critically injuring their mother in the West Bank. The victims were identified Saturday as 15-year-old Rina Dee and 20-year-old Maia Dee, the daughters of British-born Rabbi Leo Dee.  While their mother, Lucy (Lea), remains in critical condition fighting for her life, the Jewish community in the UK has expressed shock and sorrow at the brutal act of terrorism against former members of their community.    While many Jewish community leaders spoke out about the attack, the UK government has received criticism from some members of the community for its weakly-worded response to the killing of two of its own citizens.  One member of the Jewish community told Ynet that it was shocking that the UK statement didn’t even mention terrorism. “The response would be different if this happened elsewhere in the world. There is a double standard for British people killed in Israel,” he said.  The UK’s official statement read: “We are saddened to hear about the deaths of two British-Israeli citizens and the serious injuries sustained by a third individual. The UK calls for all parties across the region to de-escalate tensions.” "Tragedy for global Jewish community" Avi Abelow, family friend, said Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee are beloved and active members of their community in Efrat. "Two of the sweetest people with the sweetest children", he added. "Rabbi Leo continues to teach Torah classes in his Efrat synagogue today. All the youth of Efrat, as their families, are mourning the loss of either their personal friend or the sibling of their personal friend."  He mentioned that "Just last night the whole community got together, including many youth, for a special communal prayer gathering to pray for Lucy's recovery. The brutal Arab Muslim terrorist attack that murdered these two young, innocent Jewish women, and seriously injured their mother fighting for her life, is not just a tragedy for their family, but for the whole Efrat community and the global Jewish community.  "At the same time that another terrorist committed a terror attack in Tel Aviv, which killed an Italian tourist, and terrorist organizations are shooting rockets at Israel from Lebanon, Syria and Gaza, we are once again reminded that the Jewish people have enemies trying to kill us everywhere in our country for just being Jews living in our ancestral homeland.  "If only the UK government and other global bodies would recognize this truth, and truly give support to Israel to stop this ongoing terror war against Israel, which causes loss of life for everyone. In the meantime, as a personal friend and neighbor of the Dee family, my family, neighbors, and community will continue to assist and comfort the Dee family, as we assisted and comforted the family of our other friend and neighbor, Ari Fuld, murdered by terrorists back in 2018."

news.originalContent: Iran's powerful Revolutionary Guards warned anti-government protesters of "decisive" action if unrest over gasoline price hikes do not cease, state television reported on Monday. GREEN BAY, Wis. — Jordan Love threw a touchdown pass and also scored on a 1-yard keeper and the Green Bay Packers held Dallas’ high-powered offense in check and beat the Cowboys 23-13 in a penalty-filled game Sunday night.

Love went 23 of 41 for 276 yards to help the Packers improve to 11-1-1 in their last 13 meetings with the Cowboys, including a 40-all tie last season at Arlington, Texas. A 9-yard touchdown pass to Matthew Golden capped Green Bay’s first series and put the Packers ahead for good.

The Packers (4-2) have won three straight as they await the return of three-time Pro Bowl running back Josh Jacobs, who comes off the commissioner’s exempt list Monday. Jacobs hasn’t played all season and pleaded no contest last month to two misdemeanor charges stemming from an altercation with his then-girlfriend in May.

Green Bay intercepted Dak Prescott twice to thwart scoring opportunities. Prescott went 34 of 54 for 258 yards. He threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to Ryan Flournoy with 44 seconds left, but couldn’t connect with CeeDee Lamb on a 2-point conversion attempt.

The game featured 22 penalties — 11 by each team. Dallas had 108 penalty yards, while Green Bay had 96.

Love’s night could have been even better.

Golden dropped what would have been a 43-yard touchdown and couldn’t complete the catch on a potential 23-yard score in the second quarter. A potential 26-yard touchdown pass went in and out of Christian Watson’s hands in the third quarter, though that pass was deflected in the end zone by Dallas’ Malachi Lawrence.

The Lambeau Field fireworks started prematurely after Golden couldn’t hang on to the 23-yarder even as the officials were signaling the incompletion. Green Bay still scored a touchdown after one of those drops and settled for Trey Smack field goals after the other two.

Golden still caught six passes for 104 yards, plus the early touchdown. Love went 6 of 8 for 109 yards on that opening possession, a 90-yard drive during which the Packers withstood a couple of penalties.

Dallas (2-4) trailed 17-0 at halftime, the first time the Cowboys went scoreless in the first half of a game since Nov. 7, 2021, when they were down 16-0 in an eventual 30-16 loss to Denver.

Prescott’s two interceptions proved costly.

The Cowboys faced second-and-8 from Green Bay’s 17 when Prescott absorbed a punishing hit from Zaire Franklin while throwing an incompletion. On the next play, Evan Williams picked off a pass across the middle that was intended for Lamb.

Dallas had a first down from Green Bay’s 23 on its next drive before a holding penalty pushed it back to the 33. The Cowboys had first-and-15 from the 28 when Lamb fell on a route, enabling Packers rookie Brandon Cisse to make his first career interception.

Green Bay capitalized on that second turnover by driving 77 yards and scoring on Love’s 1-yard sneak with 23 seconds left in the half.

Dallas scored on a 1-yard run from Javonte Williams early in the third quarter. Green Bay extended the lead on a pair of field goals by Smack.

A positive development for Dallas was an improved performance from its defense, which entered the night allowing a league-high 6.4 yards per play.

Dallas’ defense held a players-only meeting in the days leading up to this game. The Cowboys also brought in veteran defensive assistant Mike Pettine to assist first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker.

Dee Winters made a diving catch late in the first quarter for Dallas’ first interception of the season. Winters then got up and weaved between multiple defenders to run over 40 yards for an apparent touchdown, but a replay review determined he was touched by Golden while still on the ground.

Cowboys: WR KaVontae Turpin left with a rib injury in the first quarter. Winters hurt his ankle in the second quarter.

Packers: CB Brandon Cisse left with a stinger in the second half.

Cowboys: At Philadelphia on Oct. 26.

Packers: At Detroit next Sunday.

news.originalContent:
Pope Leo pledges a gradual return to duties in an address to the Catholic faithful in St Peter’s Square at the Vatican.

Pope Leo XIV has thanked some 15,000 Catholic faithful gathered in St Peter’s Square during his Sunday address, his first major public appearance since lung cancer surgery.

“Now that this delicate phase is behind me, I will gradually resume my activities, always with God’s help and your prayers,” Leo said.

The 71-year-old pontiff addressed the crowd from a window overlooking the square at the Vatican, where a week ago on the same occasion of the traditional Angelus blessing, he revealed that a nodule had been found in his lung and would be surgically removed.

The operation confirmed he had adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer.

Test results to determine whether the cancer has spread are still pending.

Leo said the experience of the past week “has made me feel especially close to those facing illness and infirmity”.

He told the crowd that he had “truly felt your support” and expressed “particular gratitude to the doctors, nurses and all the staff at Gemelli Hospital” in Rome, where he was treated.

The pope paused for a moment and waved before retreating into his apartment in the Apostolic Palace.

A delegation from Africa, in Rome for a Catholic meeting, danced and ululated after the pope’s blessing.

“He was always in our prayers when he was sick, and we are happy to see him today,″ Alain Kalembu of the Democratic Republic of the Congo said. “This is an expression of our joy.”

Meanwhile, Claire Holland from Jacksonville, Florida, United States, said she felt “very blessed” to be present for the pope’s return to his flock.

There had been doubts that a planned papal voyage to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru in November would go ahead.

The Vatican’s secretary of state, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, told journalists on Friday that the pope may need to adjust the pace of his schedule “according to the condition of his health”.

But Leo’s surgeon, Stefano Margaritora, told Vatican News he believed there were “no clinical reasons why the trip should not go ahead”.

Latin Americans in the crowd in St Peter’s Square welcomed the news.

“We are all hoping for his recovery, and that he has gotten through the situation well. We know that he is OK, and we’re pleased,” Soledad Espinosa from Ecuador said.

St. John’s is honoring the late Kenny Klein this season by keeping the seat next to Coach Rick Pitino at the scorer’s table empty and adding a black band onto their jerseys with the letters, “K.K.”

The Sports Information Hall of Famer died June 25 at age 66 after a tragic episode at a dinner a few weeks prior. Klein retired in 2022 after spending nearly 40 years at Louisville. He helped out his close friend Pitino at St. John’s the past two years in the communications department.

“His wife [Donna] is going to be with us both home and away, which is big for us. On a personal level, it’s been a really horrendous summer,” Pitino said after St. John’s 104-99 exhibition victory over Rutgers in quadruple overtime at the Garden. “Not since 9/11 have I felt so sad, losing a person right in front of you who I love so much. We’ll keep honoring him. I keep thinking of him. My heart breaks for his wife. I miss him terribly.”

Throughout last season, Pitino promised Klein he would continue to coach as long as Klein stayed on with him at St. John’s.

“I believe he would’ve stayed,” Pitino said. “It’s sad, but life can be very sad. It’s a moment I’ll never forget. It’s a moment I cry about all the time. … We got to fight through it. Kenny would want us to fight through it.”

St. John’s unveiled a Ring of Honor at the Garden on Sunday. The 10 members are also part of the Legacy Honors, created in 2006. The current names are: Lou Carnesecca, Chris Mullin, Walter Berry, Mark Jackson, Sonny Dove, Tony Jackson, Joe Lapchick, Dick McGuire, Malik Sealy and Alan Seiden.

At some point this season, there will be a ceremony adding Zuby Ejiofor to the Ring of Honor. There is also talk of retiring jersey numbers, something St. John’s hasn’t previously done, according to athletic director Ed Kull.

news.originalContent:
Brazil’s president and his opponent lob a barrage of attacks on each other in debate a week before the October 25 vote.

Brazil’s President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro fired off a barrage of personal attacks during their first debate a week before a tight presidential run-off.

In a chaotic exchange on Sunday, the two men called each other “liar” multiple times, accused each other of corruption, dragged up various scandals, and clashed on issues from public security to healthcare.

Lula said Bolsonaro was “a habitual liar” and a “thug”, and physically distanced himself on stage from the candidate he called a “militiaman”, alluding to his alleged ties to Rio de Janeiro’s paramilitary groups.

Bolsonaro, who led the first-round election with 47 percent to Lula’s 45 percent, said it was better to keep Lula at a distance “because my wallet could be stolen”.

Throughout the debate, Bolsonaro, 45, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, paced behind Lula, shaking his head, smirking and scoffing as his adversary spoke.

The 80-year-old Lula, who is seeking a fourth term, demanded an explanation regarding a corruption investigation involving the older Bolsonaro, a question his opponent dodged.

The younger Bolsonaro responded by calling Lula a “clown”, and then parried by bringing up a potential corruption case involving one of the president’s sons.

Jair Bolsonaro has been under house arrest while serving a 27-year sentence connected to efforts to overturn the 2022 election, which he lost to Lula.

Flavio Bolsonaro hammered away at the top concerns of Brazilians, such as the cost of living and crime, and accused Lula of “reckless spending” to get re-elected, referring to various social measures the president has announced during the campaign.

Lula countered by asking Bolsonaro about his plans to emulate the drastic public spending cuts implemented by Argentina’s right-wing president, Javier Milei.

Bolsonaro dodged the question throughout the debate and pivoted to different topics.

When his father’s handling of the COVID-19 pandemic came up, Bolsonaro admitted that this “wasn’t an area where we saw the best results during Bolsonaro’s presidency. I’ll offer a mea culpa here.”

Lula also sought to portray his opponent as out of touch with poor Brazilians, saying Bolsonaro had never used the country’s public healthcare system or taken a bus.

“My opponent only knows about buses from books. He has never even stepped foot on one. He has no idea what the world of work is like,” Lula said.

Ahead of Sunday’s debate, supporters of each candidate gathered en masse in public to show their allegiance.

Pro-Bolsonaro crowds wearing Brazil’s national colours of yellow, green and blue packed Paulista Avenue in Sao Paulo’s financial centre, where the candidate addressed the crowd.

Lula supporters wearing red, symbolic of his Workers’ Party, filled Brasilia’s plaza of government buildings, while students backing the president protested against Bolsonaro in Rio de Janeiro.

“We need the current government to remain in power. If another government comes in, we’re, excuse my language, screwed,” said Lula supporter Sonia Maria at the Brasilia rally.

“I don’t like bandits. Out with Lula!” said Bolsonaro backer Vera de Sousa in Sao Paulo.

Also on Sunday, Brazil’s federal police asked the country’s Supreme Court to open an investigation into Bolsonaro over a money laundering accusation involving a lawyer close to him.

The presidential candidate is already under investigation for his links to Daniel Vorcaro, a disgraced former banker who financed a movie about Jair Bolsonaro’s life.

Lula spent 580 days in prison in ⁠2018 and 2019 on a corruption conviction that was later annulled over flaws in the investigation and legal proceedings.

Polls suggest a close race for the October 25 run-off, with Flavio Bolsonaro holding a slight advantage after finishing nearly 2 percentage points ahead of Lula in the first round on October 4.

Both candidates hope to engage the 33 million voters who stayed home in the first ⁠round, equal to about one in five eligible voters.

Sunday’s debate was the first between Lula and Bolsonaro after the candidates both ⁠declined previous opportunities. A second debate is scheduled for October 23, just ahead of the run-off.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

There were a handful of questionable coaching decisions and plays that were made at the end of the Giants’ 34-27 loss to the Saints that raised eyebrows.

The first was, while trailing 34-24 and driving into New Orleans territory with the ball, why the Giants didn’t kick a field goal with about three minutes remaining, to quickly cut the deficit to one score.

Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers.

They moved the ball to the New Orleans 27-yard line with 2:56 remaining with two timeouts still to use, but opted to continue to play for the touchdown.

Right tackle Marcus Mbow was then called for a false start, and then quarterback J.J. McCarthy took a sack for an 8-yard loss.

The Giants then ran two more plays before settling for a Dominic Zvada 41-yard field goal to cut the lead to 34-27 with 2:04 remaining.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh defended his actions, saying, “We went for the field goal as fast as we could, as soon as we could with a reasonable chance to make it.”

Harbaugh then said he wanted to get a touchdown there, to cut the deficit to three points.

“We had a chance there to hit a couple of shots and maybe score a touchdown,” he said. “So, at that point, we were trying to get it done by 2:13. That’s the time management there. We weren’t able to quite get it done by 2:13 with the clock and all that. But in the ideal world, you’ll get it done by 2:13, that’s what we’re shooting for.”

Harbaugh added, “We’re trying to get two scores and the two-minute warning is valuable if we can get it done. We want that two-minute warning to count for us. That’s what we’re trying to get done. That’s the goal.”

The next mistake came when Zvada’s ensuing kickoff was short enough for Bryce Lance to field it 5 yards deep and return it, thus not allowing the Giants to stop the clock at the two-minute warning.

Lance’s return ended with 1:58 on the clock, essentially taking away a free timeout from the Giants.

“You want to kick it out of the back of the end zone, that’s the goal, that’s what we were hoping to do,” Harbaugh said.

Had Zvada done that, it would have forced New Orleans to run a play before the two-minute warning.

When asked why not just kick the ball out of bounds, Harbaugh said, “We thought he could get it out of the back of the end zone.”

Zvada said, “That was a mistake I made, and I’m going to have to work on. That goal was to try to get it out of the end zone, so we stop the clock before the two-minute warning and save a timeout.”
news.content:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

There were a handful of questionable coaching decisions and plays that were made at the end of the Giants’ 34-27 loss to the Saints that raised eyebrows.

The first was, while trailing 34-24 and driving into New Orleans territory with the ball, why the Giants didn’t kick a field goal with about three minutes remaining, to quickly cut the deficit to one score.

Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers.

They moved the ball to the New Orleans 27-yard line with 2:56 remaining with two timeouts still to use, but opted to continue to play for the touchdown.

Right tackle Marcus Mbow was then called for a false start, and then quarterback J.J. McCarthy took a sack for an 8-yard loss.

The Giants then ran two more plays before settling for a Dominic Zvada 41-yard field goal to cut the lead to 34-27 with 2:04 remaining.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh defended his actions, saying, “We went for the field goal as fast as we could, as soon as we could with a reasonable chance to make it.”

Harbaugh then said he wanted to get a touchdown there, to cut the deficit to three points.

“We had a chance there to hit a couple of shots and maybe score a touchdown,” he said. “So, at that point, we were trying to get it done by 2:13. That’s the time management there. We weren’t able to quite get it done by 2:13 with the clock and all that. But in the ideal world, you’ll get it done by 2:13, that’s what we’re shooting for.”

Harbaugh added, “We’re trying to get two scores and the two-minute warning is valuable if we can get it done. We want that two-minute warning to count for us. That’s what we’re trying to get done. That’s the goal.”

The next mistake came when Zvada’s ensuing kickoff was short enough for Bryce Lance to field it 5 yards deep and return it, thus not allowing the Giants to stop the clock at the two-minute warning.

Lance’s return ended with 1:58 on the clock, essentially taking away a free timeout from the Giants.

“You want to kick it out of the back of the end zone, that’s the goal, that’s what we were hoping to do,” Harbaugh said.

Had Zvada done that, it would have forced New Orleans to run a play before the two-minute warning.

Zvada said, “That was a mistake I made, and I’m going to have to work on. That goal was to try to get it out of the end zone, so we stop the clock before the two-minute warning and save a timeout.”

First, the officials surprised Andrew Thomas by pulling him off the field.

Then, the Giants coaches surprised him by keeping him on the bench.

Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers.

Thomas, one of the best left tackles in the NFL, didn’t return to the field in the fourth quarter after clearing a concussion evaluation on the sideline ordered by the independent spotter Sunday in a 34-27 loss to the Saints.

“That was interesting,” said Thomas, who is playing through an injured groin despite limited practice time. “The series before, I got up a little slow. When I went out there the next drive, they said I had to do the concussion protocol testing.”

Thomas looked antsy to get back in, but the Giants, who were rallying from a 24-point fourth-quarter deficit, were stuck with rookie J.C. Davis in his first career game.

Thomas did not get an explanation for the change.

“That was the coach’s decision,” Thomas said. “I listen to what the coach says.”

Thomas was not the only injury-related blow dealt to the Giants on Sunday. CB Greg Newsome II suffered a concussion and did not return.

WR Darnell Mooney (neck) was sidelined, leaving the Giants with three healthy receivers.

RG Sisi Mauigoa needed a postgame X-ray on an unspecified body part.

“I’m feeling good,” Mauigoa said, indicating he will be on the field again soon.

RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) was a surprise scratch after he was limited in Friday’s practice. Marcus Mbow started in his place.

Jason Pinnock and Ar’Darius Washington rotated at the safety position next to Jevón Holland with Tyler Nubin (neck) sidelined.

Pinnock forced a fumble that turned momentum when the Giants were down 34-10 with about 9:40 left in the fourth quarter.

“It’s in us to come back,” Pinnock said. “We’re more than capable.”

The only game in which a Giants quarterback had more fourth-quarter passing yards than J.J. McCarthy’s 243 on Sunday was when Eli Manning threw for 254 in a 36-25 loss against the Seahawks on Oct. 9, 2011.

McCarthy entered the game with about 11:31 left in the game after Jameis Winston threw his second interception. McCarthy went 11-for-21 with 243 yards passing, 26 rushing yards, a touchdown pass and an interception.
